la:verb:perspicio.html:
perspĭcĭo, spexi, spectum, 3, v. a.,
to look or see through, to look into, look at.
Lit.: quo non modo non intrari, sed ne perspici quidem posset,: eas (epistulas) ego oportet perspiciam, corrigam: tum denique edentur, to lookthrough, read through, : ut prae densitate arborum perspici caelum vix posset,to look at the sky,.—
Transf., to look closely at, to view, examine, inspect: domum,: villam,: operis perspiciendi causā venire,: minimis id granis constat, ut vix perspici quaedam possint,are scarcely visible,.—With a rel.-clause: perspicito prius, quid intus agatur,.— Neutr.: in legem,.—
Trop., to perceive, note, observe, explore, prove, ascertain, etc.: res gestas funditus,: cum se ipse perspexerit,: sed tu perspice rem et pertenta,; cf. : hoc, quaeso, perspicite atque cognoscite,: aliquid conjecturā,to guess,: cujus virtutem hostes, misericordiam victi, fidem ceteri perspexerunt,: nollem accidisset tempus, in quo perspicere posses, quanti te facerem,: quidam saepe in parvā pecuniā perspiciuntur, quam sint leves,: perpaucos, quorum in se fidem perspexerat, relinquere in Galliā decrevit,: videbitis et non perspicietis,.—With object-clause: perspicio nihili meam vos facere gratiam,; cf. : perspiciebant enim in Hortensii sententiam multis partibus plures ituros,.—Pass. with nom. and inf., .— Hence, perspectus, a, um, P. a., clearly perceived, evident, well known: ars rebus cognitis penitusque perspectis continetur,; cf. ; : virtus alicujus experta atque perspecta,: benevolentia mihi perspectissima,.—Adv.: per-spectē, intelligently, sensibly: ut docte et perspecte sapit,.

senses: to prevail upon, persuade or induce to do something
la:verb:persuadeo.html:
per-suādĕo, si, sum, 2, v. a.,
to bring over by talking, to convince of the truth of any thing, to persuade (cf. convinco).
In gen., constr. absol., with an obj.-clause and dat., rarely with acc. of the person: oratoris officium est dicere ad persuadendum accommodate,: imprimis hoc volunt persuadere, non interire animas,: velim tibi ita persuadeas, me, etc.,: hoc cum mihi non modo confirmasset, sed etiam persuasisset,: ne si forte de paupertate non persuaseris, sit aegritudini concedendum,; Hor S. 1, 6, 8; : quis te persuasit, Enn. ap. (p. 175, n. 4 Vahl.).—Pass. pers. (rare): cum animus auditoris persuasus esse videtur ab eis, qui, etc.,: si persuasus auditor fuerit,, § 10: si scit et persuasus est, quid irascitur, etc., Caecil. ap. .—Pass. impers.: corrupti sunt quibus persuasum sit foedissimum hostem justissimo bello prosequi,: mihi persuaderi numquam potuit, animos ... vivere, etc.,. persuasum habere, v. P. a. infra.—
In partic., to prompt, induce, prevail upon, persuade to do any thing (class.); usually constr. with alicui, ut, or ne; rarely (and post-Aug.) aliquem or with an obj.-clause: persuasit nox, amor, adulescentia,: metuebat ne sibi persuaderes, ut, etc.,: huic magnis praemiis pollicitationibusque persuadent, uti, etc.,: huic Albinus persuadet, regnum ab senatu petat,: duo sunt tempora, quibus aliquid contra Caesarem Pompeio suaserim, unum, ne, etc.... alterum ne, etc.... quorum si utrumvis persuasissem, etc.,: numquam tamen haec felicitas illi persuasit neglegentiam,led him into negligence,, praef. 5: omnia nobis mala solitudo persuadet,: persuasit ei tyrannidis finem facere,: nec arare terram aut expectare annum tam facile persuaseris, etc.,: quis Romanis primus persuaserit navem conscendere?: frigidāque etiam hibernis algoribus persuasit,: aliquā die te persuadeam, ut, etc.,.—Impers. pass.: his persuaderi, ut, etc., non poterat,: persuasum est facere,; cf.: tibi quidquam persuaderi potuisse,: tibi persuasum habere, for sibi persuaderi: ea loca provinciae adjungere sibi persuasum habebant,; v. Zumpt, Gr. § 407, n. 1; § 634.—Hence, P. a.: persuāsus, a, um, fixed, established, settled.—Sup.: quod mihi persuasissimum est, Brut. ap. .—Esp., in phrase persuasum habere, to be convinced, regard as settled: quia persuasum habuerunt, animas hominum immortalis esse,: comperi persuasissimum habuisse eum, with obj.clause, : at nos e diverso fumi amaritudine vetustatem indui persuasum habemus,: persuasum habeo posse fieri ut, etc.,; ;

la:verb:perspecto.html:
perspecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
id.
. *
To look at or behold to the end: quinquennale certamen gymnicum perspectavit,.—
To look through, look all about: otiose perspecta aedis, ut lubet,.

la:verb:perscribo.gloss: to write out; to write in full or in detail
senses: to write out; to write in full or in detail
la:verb:perscribo.html:
per-scrībo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a.
Lit., to write in full or at length, to write out, to write without abbreviations (cf.: conscribo, compono): verbo non perscripto, not being written in full, Tiro Tullius ap. : in M. Catonis quartā Origine ita perscriptum est,written out, written in full,: notata, non perscripta erat summa,: est circa perscribendas vel paucioribus litteris notandas voces studium necessarium,.—
Transf.
To write a full description of, to write in full or at length, to write out: nunc velim mihi plane perscribas, quid videas,: de meis rebus ad Lollium perscripsi,: hoc perscriptum in monumentis veteribus reperietis, ut, etc.,: res populi Romani a primordio urbis, Liv. praef. init.: versum puris verbis,. —
To write or note down; to enter, register, : quoniam nondum perscriptum est senatūs consultum, ex memoriā vobis, quid senatus censuerit exponam,: in tabulas publicas ad aerarium perscribenda curavit,; .—Hence, tabulae ubi aera perscribantur usuraria, i. e. inscribed, but never paid out, .—Esp., of entering in an account-book: falsum nomen,.—
To write a full account of to any one, to announce, relate, or describe in writing or by letter: rem gestam in Eburonibus perscribit,; : perscribit in litteris hostes ab se discessisse,: orationem alicui,: omnia,.—
To make over in writing, to assign any thing to any one: argentum perscripsi illis, quibus debui,: pecuniam,; cf. : si quid usurae nomine numeratum aut perscriptum fuisset,; cf. .—
To draw a line across, to cross a written character = διαγράφειν (post-class.): as nummus est libralis et per I perscriptam notatur †: dupondius nummus est bilibris per duas II perscriptas H, etc. ... denarius quoque decem librarum nummus per X perscriptam notatur *, P.

la:noun:persona.html:
persōna, ae,
f [acc. to Gabius Bassus ap. , from per-sŏno, to sound through, with the second syllable lengthened].
A mask, esp. that used by players, which covered the whole head, and was varied according to the different characters to be represented (syn. larva), : personam tragicam forte vulpis viderat,: personam capiti detrahere,: persona adicitur capiti,. The masks were usually made of clay: cretea persona,, cf. . And sometimes of the bark of wood: oraque corticibus sumunt horrenda cavatis,: ut tragicus cantor ligno tegit ora cavato, Prud. adv . The opening for the mouth was very large: personae pallentis hiatum formidat infans,: personis uti primus coepit Roscius Gallus praecipuus histrio, quod oculis obversis erat, nec satis decorus in personis nisi parasitus pronunciabat, P. Heads with such masks were used as ornaments for water-spouts, fountains, etc.: Butades figulus primus personas tegularum extremis imbricibus imposuit, quae inter initia prostypa vocavit,: personae, e quarum rostris aqua salire solet,: mulier nempe ipsa videtur, non personā loqui, a mask, a masked person, Juv 3, 96.—
Transf., a personage, character, part, represented by an actor: parasiti persona,: sub personā militis,: (tragici) nihil ex personā poëtae dixerunt,.—Hence,
Also, transf. beyond the scenic lang., in gen., the part or character which any one sustains in the world (class.): (ego), qui non heroum veteres casus fictosque luctus velim imitari atque adumbrare dicendo, neque actor sim alienae personae, sed auctor meae,: quam magnum est personam in re publicā tueri principis,: personam sustinere,: personam, quam mihi tempus et res publica imposuit,imposed upon me,; cf.: agenda est persona quam mihi miles imposuit,; : partes lenitatis et misericordiae semper egi libenter: illam vero gravitatis severitatisque personam non appetivi, sed a re publicā mihi impositam sustinui,: petitoris personam capere, accusatoris deponere,: personam suscipere,: gravissimam personam sustinere,: personam tenere,: personam gerere,: abjectā quaestoriā personā comitisque assumptā,: fateantur in Maeandrii personā esse expressam speciem civitatis,: id Cicero suā ipsā personā frequentissime praecipit,in his own name,: cetera quae sunt a me in secundo libro de Oratore per Antonii personam disputata, B. and K. (dub.; al. ex personā): ex tuā personā enumerare possis, ut, etc.,: nihil ex personā poëtae disserunt,; ; so ; ; : sub personā Paridis,: so ; : alienam personam ferre,: non hominibus tantum,

sed et rebus persona demenda est et reddenda facies sua, : hanc personam induisti: agenda est,.—Hence,

A human being who performs any function, plays any part, a person, personage: ut mea persona semper aliquid videretur habere populare,, D, § 7: ecquae pacifica persona desideretur,: hujus Staleni persona, populo jam nota atque perspecta,; : induxi senem disputantem, quia nulla videbatur aptior persona,: Laelii persona,: certis personis et aetatibus,to people of a certain standing and of a certain age,: minoribus quoque et personis et rebus,to persons and things of less importance,; : nulla distantia personarum,: personarum acceptio,; cf. : ipse suā lege damnatus, cum, substituta filii personā, amplius quingentorum jugerum possideret,: denique haec fuit altera persona Thebis, sed tamen secunda, ita ut proxima esset Epaminondae,the second chief personage,.—
So of persons, opp. to things and actions: ut rerum, ut personarum dignitates ferunt,.—
Law t. t., a being having legal rights and obligations (including the state, etc.; not including slaves; cf. Sandars ad introd. § 37; 1, 3 prooem.): omne jus quo utimur, vel ad personas pertinet vel ad res vel ad actiones,; prooem.—
A human being in gen., a person (post-Aug. and rare): continuantes unum quodque (praenomen) per trinas personas,: cum dira et foedior omni Crimine persona est,.—
In the grammarians, a person: quom item personarum natura triplex esset, qui loqueretur, ad quem, de quo, Müll.; so , § 32 et saep.

la:noun:perscriptio.html:
perscriptĭo, ōnis, f.
perscribo
.
A writing down, an entry in a book, an official recording: perscriptionum et liturarum adversaria,; : falsae perscriptiones,; .—
A making over in writing, an assignment, : haec pactio non verbis sed nominibua et perscriptionibus facta est,.

la:verb:persequor.gloss: to follow perseveringly, continue to follow; search through; pursue
senses: to follow perseveringly, continue to follow; search through; pursue
to pursue, chase, hunt; to avenge, take vengeance upon someone or something; prosecute; to persecute
to seek to obtain, strive after, seek out
to follow the teaching or example of someone, imitate
to follow up with action, execute, bring about, do, accomplish
to follow, take down, minute down, keep pace with, record
la:verb:persequor.html:
per-sĕquor, cūtus and quūtus, 3,
v. dep. a. and n. (act. collat. form of the imperat. persece for perseque, Poët. ap. ).
Act., to follow perseveringly, to follow after, continue to follow, pursue.
Lit.
In gen.: ille servolum Jubet illum persequi,; : si vis persequi vestigiis,: certum est persequi,: me in Asiam persequens,: (persequens dicit perseverationem sequentis ostendens. Persequitur enim qui non desinit sequi, Don. ad h. l.): aliquem,: exercitum,: cursim,: Hortensium ipsius vestigiis,: quā, aut terrā aut mari, persequar eum, qui, etc.,: vestigia alicujus,; : hanc persecuta mater orare incipit,.—With inf. (poet.): atqui non ego te tigris ut aspera ... frangere persequor,.—
In partic.
To follow after, press upon, chase, pursue: fugientes usque ad flumen persequuntur,: bello,: deterrere hostes a persequendo,: feras,: beluas,.—
To go through a place in pursuit of any thing, to search through: omnes solitudines,. —
Transf., to follow up, come up with, overtake: quo ego te ne persequi quidem possem triginta diebus,; : mors et fugacem persequitur virum,.—
Trop.
In gen., to follow perseveringly, to pursue any thing: omnes vias persequar,: viam,: eas artes,.—
In partic.
With the accessory notion of striving after, to pursue, hunt after, seek to obtain, strive after, = appetere, affectare: quis est, qui utilia non studiosissime persequatur?: ego mihi alios deos penates persequar,: Pl. Tene priusquam hinc abeo savium. Ph. Si quidem mi hercle regnum detur, numquam id potius persequar, : hereditates,: hereditates aut syngraphas,: cujusquemodi voluptates,: ego meum jus persequar, I will pursue or assert my right, ; : persequendi juris sui potestas,: bona tua repetere ac persequi lite atque judicio,: possumus rem nostram persequi,: cum tribunus plebis poenas a seditioso cive per bonos viros judicio persequi vellet,sought to obtain,.—
With inf., to hasten, be eager (rare): nec scimus quam in partem ingredi persequamur,.—
To follow, be a follower of; to imitate, copy after a person or thing as a guide or pattern: si vero Academiam veterem persequamur,: sectam et instituta alicujus,: ego neglectā barbarorum inscitiā te persequar,; : ut, quae maxime excellant in eo, quem imitabitur, ea diligentissime persequatur,.—
To pursue, proceed against, prosecute; to revenge, avenge, take vengeance upon a person or thing: aliquem bello,: aliquem judicio,: alicujus injurias ulcisci ac persequi,; so, injuriam,; ; cf. Kritz ad , 5: mortem alicujus,: de persequendis inimicitiis,: Trebonii mortem,; ; : adulterium,.—
To persecute for religious belief or practice (eccl. Lat.), ; ; ; et saep.—
To follow in writing, to take down, minute down: celeritate scribendi, quae dicerentur persequi,: multa diserte dixit, quae notarius persequi non potuit,.—
To follow up with action, to follow out, perform, execute, bring about, do, accomplish, etc.: hoc, ut dico, factis persequar,: erus quod imperavit persequi,: imperium patris,: ex usu quod est, id persequar,: mandata,: si idem extrema persequitur qui inchoavit,: vitam inopem et vagam,to lead,.—Absol.: sed tamen ibo et persequar,will go and obey,. —
In partic., to follow out in speech or writing, to set forth, treat of, relate, recount, describe, explain, etc.: aliquid voce,: dum rationes Persequor,set forth, treat of, discuss the reasons,: quae versibus persecutus est Ennius,: philosophiam Latinis litteris,: aliquid scripturā,: obscenas voluptates,: res Hannibalis,: has res in eo libro,: quae persequerer, si commemorare possem sine dolore,: da te in sermonem et persece Et confice, etc., Poët. ap. .—*
Neutr., to follow or come after: exacta vindemia gramine persecuto,when the grass has grown again,.!*? In a pass. signif. (post-class.): illa se in mare praecipitavit, ne persequeretur, dub.—Hence, persĕquens, entis, P. a., used as subst. *
A pursuer, practiser: flagitii,.— *
A revenger, avenger: inimicitiarum persequentissimus,.
la:verb:persequor.inflection: cūtus and quūtus, 3, v. dep. a., n.

la:verb:persono.gloss: to sound through and through, resound, ring
senses: to sound through and through, resound, ring
to make a sound on a musical instrument, play, sound
to fill with sound, make resound
la:verb:persono.html:
per-sŏno, ŭi, ĭtum, 1 (
perf. personavit, : personasse, Prud. στεφ. 34 praef.), v. n. and a.
Neutr.
To sound through and through, to resound: cum domus cantu et cymbalis personaret,: ut cotidiano cantu vocum et nervorum et tibiarum nocturnisque conviviis tota vicinitas personet,; : domus Molossis Personuit canibus,: ploratu lamentisque et planctibus tota regia personabat,: ab aetheris personat axe fragor,: tuba,.—
To make a sound on a musical instrument, to sound, play: citharā Iopas Personat,: cymbalis,: buccinis,.—
Act.
To fill with sound or noise, to make resound (class.): Cerberus haec regna latratu Personat,: aequora conchā,: aures hujusmodi vocibus, ; so, aurem,to bawl in one's ear,: ille humi prostraverat corpus, gemitu ejulatuque totam personans regiam,: pulpita socco,to play in comedy,: mons choris Aegipanum undique personatur,.—
To cry out, call aloud (rare but class.): illae vero non loquuntur solum, verum etiam personant, huc unius mulieris libidinem esse prolapsam,: quas res isti in angulis personant,: totam inde per urbem personat, ut, etc.,; Tac.A. 14, 15; .—
To sound or blow upon an instrument (post-class.): personavit classicum,gave the signal for attack,.
la:verb:persono.inflection: ŭi, ĭtum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:perseco.html:
per-sĕco, cui, ctum, 1, v. a.,
to cut up, exlirpate; to cut out, excise; trop.: vitium,: rei publicae vomicas, Auct. ap. : rerum naturas,to dissect, lay bare the secrets of nature,. (For perseca, , read persece; v. persequor, I. fin.)

senses: to pay, pay out or render
to perform, accomplish, fulfill an obligation or task
la:verb:persolvo.html:
per-solvo, solvi, sŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to release or discharge completely; acc. to the signif. of the simple verb.
To pay, pay out: stipendium militibus,: pecuniam alicui,: pecuniam ab aliquo,to pay by a draft on any one,: aes alienum alienis nominibus suis copiis, to pay the debts of others, Cat. ap. ; : legatā cum fide,: veteranis promissa praemia,.—
Transf., in gen., to pay, give, show, render what is due to another: quod relicum restat, volo persolvere,: alicui laborum praemia pro me,: hanc tibi animam pro morte Daretis,; : grates,to render thanks,; cf.: meritam dis immortalibus gratiam,: honorem dis, topay due honor to the gods by sacrifices, : vota,to fulfil,; ; : velim reliquum, quod est promissi ac muneris tui mihi persolvas,; : quod huic promisi, id ei persolvere,: persolvere justa,to pay due honors to the dead,; so : poenas, to suffer punishment: poenas dis hominibusque meritas debitasque persolvat,: mihi sanguine poenas Persolves,.—Without the dat.: ea (pars civitatis) princeps poenas persolvit,; cf.: supplicia persolvit, —On the contrary: poenae alicui ab omnibus persolutae,imparted, inflicted by all,; so, mortem alicui,i. e. to kill, put to death,: persolvi primae epistulae,have answered,: NATVRAE DEBITVM,to die,; so, DEBITVM,. —*
To unravel, solve, explain: si hoc mihi ζητημα persolveris, magnā me molestiā liberaris, .

la:verb:persevero.gloss: to abide by; to adhere to
senses: to abide by; to adhere to
to continue steadfastly: to persist, to persevere
la:verb:persevero.html:
persĕvēro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[perseverus].
Neutr., to abide by or adhere to strictly; to continue steadfastly, to persist, persevere in any thing (class.; syn.: persisto, permaneo).
With in and abl.: perseveras tu quidem et in tuā vetere sententiā permanes,; so, in suā sententiā,: in vitiis,: in errore,: in eo perseveravit, jus publicano non dicere,; ; : nobiscum,continuing with us,.—
Impers. pass.: perseveratum in irā est,; : in eo perseverandum putabat,.—
Act., to go on or proceed with steadily, to persist, persevere in any thing (class.); usually constr with an object-clause; rarely with acc. or abl.
With inf.: injuriam facere,: aliquem conservare, Curius ap. : bello persequi,.—With acc. and inf: cum Orestes perseveraret, se esse Orestem,stuck to it,; so, cum id facturos se perseverarent,.—
With acc.: neque te ipsum id perseverare et transigere potuisse,: religiosam observantiam, (96).—In the pass.: ob haec illi quatriduo perseverata inedia est,—
With abl.: bellis continuis perseverare,.—Hence, persĕvērans, antis, P. a., persevering; with abl.: perseverantior caedendis (hostibus), (Madv. caedendi).—Absol.: perseverantissimus sui cultus,ext.: perseverantissimum studium, Col. praef. 1, § 19: pertinaciter perseverans, Jul. : valetudo,: perseverantissima pietas,.—Adv.: persĕvēranter, perseveringly: tueri,: tacere,.—Comp.: perseverantius saevire,.—Sup.: aliquem perseverantissime diligere, (dub.; Keil, persevera).
la:verb:persevero.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:perstringo.gloss: to bind tightly together; to draw together or up, contract
senses: to bind tightly together; to draw together or up, contract
to graze, graze against a thing
to make blunt by grazing against, to make dull, to dull
to touch or wound slightly with words
to touch on slightly, glance over, narrate briefly
la:verb:perstringo.html:
per-stringo, nxi, ctum, 3, v. a.
To bind tightly together; to draw together, draw up, contract: vitem,: stomachus nimio rigore perstrictus,; .—
To graze, graze against a thing.
Lit.: femur,: solum aratro,to plough slightly,: portam vomere,to graze against, dub. (al. praestr-).—
Transf., To blunt by grazing against, to make dull, to dull: minaci murmure aures,to stun, deafen,: juvenem multo perstringunt lumine, (but for perstringere oculos, aciem, etc., cf. praestringo).—
Trop.
To seize: horror ingens spectantes perstringit,; ; cf. .—
In partic.
To touch or wound slightly with words; to blame, censure, reprimand, reprove (class.): alicujus voluntatem asperioribus facetiis,: aliquem vocis libertate,: aliquem suspicione,: aliquem oblique,: cultum habitumque alicujus lenibus verbis,: modice perstricti,: ad perstringendos mulcendosque militum animos,.—
In speaking, to touch slightly, to glance over, to narrate briefly: leviter transire ac tantummodo perstringere unamquamque rem,: quod meis omnibus litteris in Pompeianā laude perstrictus est (Crassus),belittled, slighted,: perquam breviter perstringere atque attingere,: celeriter perstringere reliquum vitae cursum,: summatim,.

la:noun:perseverantia.html:
persĕvērantĭa, ae, f.
persevero
,
steadfastness, constancy, perseverance (syn. pertinacia): perseverantia est in ratione bene consideratā stabilis et perpetua permansio,; : disputandum est, aliud an idem sit pertinacia et perseverantia,: nautarum,; .—
Transf., objectively, long continuance, tediousness: belli,.

la:adv:persaepe.html:
per-saepe, adv.,
very often, very frequently: quod persaepe fit,: frons, oculi, voltus persaepe mentiuntur,: persaepe velut qui Junonis sacra ferret,; .—In tmesi: per pol saepe peccas,.

la:verb:persto.html:
per-sto, stĭti, stātum (
fut. part. perstaturus, ), 1, v. n., to stand firmly, continue standing.
Lit. (rare): frenatis equis equites diem totum perstabant,: exercitus a mane usque ad horam X. diei perstiterunt, Auct. B Afr. 61 in limine,.—
Transf., to remain steadfast or constant, to last, endure: nihil est toto quod perstet in orbe: cuncta

fluunt, ; : laurea flaminibus, quae toto perstitit anno, Tollitur,: rabies,.—

Trop., to stand fast or firm, to hold out, continue, persevere, persist in any thing (class.; syn.: persevero, permaneo); usually constr. with in and abl.: negant posse, et in eo perstant,: in pravitate,: in impudentiā,: in sententiā,; ; : in incepto, Drak. N. cr.; 8, 34, 4; 10, 13, 10: in pertinaci simulatione inopiae,: in bello,: in iisdem dictis,.—Impers. pass.: ut in decreto perstaretur,: si perstaretur in bello,: optimates in Romanā societate perstandum censebant,.—
Absol.: nunc quoque mens eadem perstat mihi,: talia perstabat memorans,: persta atque obdura,: perstitit Narcissus,persisted in his determination,.—
With inf.: aut pertinacissimus fueris, si perstiteris ad corpus ea, quae dixi, referre, Madv. ad loc. 3 (B. and K.; al. perstiteris in eo): persto condere semen humo,: perstas non cedere terris,; .

la:verb:persentio.html:
per-sentĭo, si, sum, 4, v. a.,
to perceive plainly.
; .—
To feel deeply: pectore curas,.

la:noun:perspicuitas.html:
perspĭcŭĭtas, ātis, f.
perspicuus
,

la:noun:Perseus.html:
Perseus, ĕi and ĕos (acc., Persea, ), m., = Περσεύς.
Son of Jupiter and Danăē, abandoned by his grandfather Acrisius, but rescued and brought up by Polydectes, king of Seriphus. When grown up, he undertook, at the instigation of Polydectes, an expedition against the islands of the Gorgons, and received from Vulcan a sickle-shaped sword, from Mercury winged shoes, and from Minerva a shield and the flying horse Pegasus. Thus armed, he killed and cut off the head of Medusa, whose look turned every thing into stone. On his way back, he, by means of it, turned into stone a sea-monster to which Andromeda, the daughter of Cepheus, was exposed, and married her. Their son Perses became the progenitor of the Persians. After his death, Perseus was placed among

the constellations, ; ; ; ; ; (3, 28), 4; 2, 28 (3, 24), 22; .—

Hence,
Per-sēus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Perseus, Persean, . Perseos alter in Argos scinditur,i. e. where Perseus's grandfather, Acrisius, reigned,: Persei culmina montis,the mountain where Perseus first mounted Pegasus,: Persea Tarsos,founded by Perseus,: Babylon,.—
Per-sēïus, a, um, Persean: Perseia castra sequi,to fight in his army,.—
The last king of Macedonia, v. Perses, IV.
